utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 4, I think, is the witness Mr. Re indicated just a moment ago, when mentioning her name, is not a protected witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Earlier I said we would call them witness and then a number and that would ... Okay. Then we'll hear from you as soon as possible on that. Then finally I have to give you the full decision on protective measures for Witness 38. On the 6th of March -- on the 6th of March, 2007, the Prosecution applied for the protective measures pseudonym and face and voice distortion for Witness 38. According to the Prosecution, the witness has been receiving death threats, directed both against the witness and the witness's family. The threats came mainly through telephone calls, and the threats are ongoing. The witness has, in particular, expressed serious concern for the safety of family members. On the 7th of March, yesterday, the Defence has informed the Trial Chamber that it does not oppose the application. The party seeking protective measures for a witness, which in this case is the Prosecution, must demonstrate an objectively grounded risk to the security or welfare of the witness or the witness's family, should it become known that the witness has given evidence before the Tribunal. This standard can be satisfied by showing that a threat was made against the witness or the witness's family, or by demonstrating a combination of the following three factors: One, the witness's testimony may antagonise persons who reside in a specific territory; two, the witness or his or her family live or work in that territory, have property in that territory, or have concrete plans to return to live in the territory; and three, there exists an unstable security situation in that territory which is particularly unfavourable to witnesses who appear before the Tribunal. In the present case, clear and direct threats have been directed against Witness 38. The Trial Chamber accepts that the witness's fear is genuine and objectively based, and that there is a risk that if the testimony of the witness were to be made public, physical harm might result to the witness or the witness's family. The Trial Chamber therefore grants the Prosecution's request for pseudonym and face and voice distortion. This concludes the Trial Chamber's decision on protective measures for Witness 38. I have no further procedural matters. If none of the parties want to raise one, we'll ask the usher to -- first of all, to see whether all the technical measures for protective measures are in place, and then invite the usher to call the witness. But I see that -- yes.

I do understand that it has not happened, but pseudonym sheets are exhibits and should be uploaded. utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Everyone in this courtroom will call you Witness 38. That is because you are testifying under a pseudonym, not under your own name. Apart from that protective measure, we also have put in place face distortion and voice distortion. That means anyone outside this courtroom, on the screens, on television, could not see your own face, cannot hear your own voice. It's all distorted. If you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If, while answering a question, if you would be hesitant because you would fear that by answering the question you would reveal your own identity, you always can ask me, then, to go into closed session for a moment so that the information you give would, under those circumstances, also be protected.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These are the protective measures in place. You asked for them; they have been granted by the Chamber. And everyone will do its utmost best to make them effective. utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated. You will first be examined by Mr. Di Fazio, who is counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Di Fazio, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just very briefly, again don't mention names, you see, I think it's now agreed, that your name appears at the top? Do you agree? I have to hear you say yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Underneath that, is that your father's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And underneath that is your sister's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Followed by your sister-in-law's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And underneath that, the first two names of her children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And then the name of your -- the first name of your step-mother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes. I see the name. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. And then the name of your uncle, and then followed finally by the name of your aunt?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, we now need to go into private session very briefly while I deal some career aspects of this woman that might tend to identify her.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, your face and voice is still hidden, but the content of your testimony is now public again. Please proceed, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I want to know about the population, the people who were living in Junik. Can you tell us if there were any families living in Junik of Roma or Egyptian ethnicity, who referred to themselves as Roma or Egyptian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Of Roma ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, would you please switch off your microphone if the witness answers the questions, because your microphone does not give any distortion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might at this time, Your Honour, since there's a break. I'm concerned that we may be seeing a number of leading questions. Thus far I don't think there's really any objection because we've been dealing with matters that need to be gotten through kind of rapidly. But when we reach some sensitive areas, I trust that we will not see that. And I don't know how you wish for us to deal with it in terms of the flow of examination? Because I don't want to be standing up all the time if such questions are occurring.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It very much depends on the topic and therefore you're invited to -- to identify the moments where leading the witness would really be of potential influence to -- and, of course, you could say every leading question, but it's just a matter of asking yourself to what extent there's a need to object, and then, of course, we'll decide on any objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If I may help my learned colleague, I think I might have an idea of what might be the controversial topics in this testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In your house that you lived in, in Junik, did you have a view of the main street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I want you to turn your attention to the first few months of 1998, and I want to ask you if you ever saw vehicles driving up and down the main street in the first few months of 1998.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you ever see vehicles driving up and down the main street at night-time in the first few months of 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In May of 1998, early May of 1998, were you still living in your house in Junik with a view of that main street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you ever, in early May of 1998, see a collection of cars in that street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you remember about when that was in May of 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Don't answer this if you can't. Can you give us an approximate date in May? Was it in the middle, perhaps the beginning or perhaps at the end of May, or you don't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: It was sometime around mid-May, the 6th or the 7th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And on this occasion that you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Early May.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right, thank you. And on this occasion that you saw these cars, can you tell us how many cars you saw, this collection of cars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: There were about four cars and two vans.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And about what time of day was it that you saw these -- this collection of cars and vans?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: At night.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were there men in the cars or in the vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you know or recognise any of the men in the vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Except one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I understand that you are saying you understood one; is that -- my understanding correct? You knew one, one of them; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No, I apologise. Actually, two.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. They're not related to you, are they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you understand them to be inhabitants of Junik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What were their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Shkelzen Pepshi and Aslan Luluni.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And what ethnicity were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What did you see -- what happened when the cars arrived and you saw them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: There was another group waiting there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: A group of men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And where were you looking from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I was looking out the window, from the direction of the window, on the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What did the men in the cars do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: They got out of the vehicles and started distributing weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: To whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: To that other group that was -- that had been waiting for them to come.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And about how many people were in that group that had been waiting for them to come, as you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I cannot recall the number, but there were quite a few.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you see the actual weapons themselves? Did you actually lay eyes on weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You may or may not be able to answer this; do not if you're not sure. Can you tell us what sort of weaponry it was that was being distributed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I don't know much about that, but I shall try. There were semi-automatic rifles; automatic rifles; there were pistols; there were other kinds of weapons, quite a lot of them, in those cars.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I take it the distribution process finished at some point. What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Then they went in the direction of Pesh, which is a settlement near Junik.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who went in that direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Would you please repeat that question. I did not quite understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. You've told us that there were some vehicles that arrived, a collection of cars and some vans, and there were men in that set of vehicles. You've also told us that there was a group of men to whom weapons were distributed from those vehicles, or from that group of men who arrived in the vehicles.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: After the distribution of weapons had been completed, what did the men in the cars do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: They went out of the cars. They started shooting. They started celebrating.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you actually see that with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: From your window in your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. And what about the group of men who had been there when the cars -- who met the cars? What did they do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: They got weapons and they set off in the direction of Pesh, which is a small settlement in Junik.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. And did the cars eventually depart and go away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you see any of the men again that night, either the men who had arrived in the cars or the group that met them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No, not that night. I went to bed. But that night they threw stones at my window and broke the windows -- the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who threw the stones, do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you take any action in respect of that? Did you do anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What did you do about the stones being thrown at your windows?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I went to see the president of the democratic party in Junik.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman named Qemajl Shalja?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was he a resident of Junik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Think back to this night when the cars arrived and you saw another group of men waiting, and you've told us about how the weapons were -- were handed out.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is that -- is that the night that the stone or stones were thrown at your windows? Did it happen on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you ever see Qemajl, the man you know as Qemajl Shalja, talking or giving a speech in the village of Junik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, on the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know who he was with when he gave the speech, or spoke?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: He was with the president of the democratic party and quite a few other people around him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were there other local inhabitants, local residents, from the village gathered to hear what was being said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you go and listen to what was being said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes. I approached them but I wasn't that close to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Could you hear what was being said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: About how many people were gathered, listening to what was being said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: It was a large number of people. I cannot tell you exactly how many, but there were many people.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And can you tell us what Mr. Shalja said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Mr. Shalja said that he had come from Glodjane, where he had had a six-month training course, and he was responsible for gathering young men, training them, and distributing weapons to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did he mention any entities, any organisations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: What do you mean? Which organisation?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did Mr. Shalja say who he had been training with in Glodjane?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: He said the headquarters was in Glodjane and he had been trained by other people who were superior to him. But he didn't name them; he only used code-names.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did he give you any explanation of the headquarters? Did he ever say it was the headquarters of any particular organisation? Did you -- headquarters of what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: He explained to them about the headquarters. I just overhead what he said. And he said that it was training about warfare and that he was supposed to train other young people who knew nothing about waging war about using weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you see any weapons on this occasion? You've told us about the night before --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- now you're telling us about the next day, okay, when Mr. Shalja was there giving his talk to the villagers. Did you see weapons on this occasion when he was talking to the villagers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What sort of quantities of weapons did you see? Can you give us an idea? One or two guns? Was it a lot? A few? How many?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I saw only his weapons. He had everything from a semi-automatic rifle to the radio, but they didn't distribute weapons there that day. They must have distributed weapons elsewhere. I just saw the gear that he had, and he had all of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How was he dressed? Think carefully about this. How was he dressed? What was the colour of his clothing and what did he have on his body and around him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: He was wearing multi-coloured clothes. On his right-hand side -- in fact, it was the greenish camouflage uniform similar to that of the Army of Yugoslavia. On the right-hand side he had a UCK sign, that's the KLA insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, have you ever heard of this UCK, or KLA, insignia? Have you ever -- had you ever seen it or heard of it before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I had seen it when the policemen had captured some of them. They were taking away some people who were wearing that. And they had on the wall a kind of chart showing those insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, which wall are you talking about? Was it a wall -- do I understand that you're talking about some wall close to this man Shalja, as he was talking, giving his speech? (redacted) They had this chart showing all sorts of emblems and insignia, so we knew what they looked like.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Would Your Honours just bear with me for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I want to show the witness a symbol, a piece of paper with a symbol on it. It's not in e-court and hasn't been distributed to the Defence yet, but I don't think it's going to be controversial, and I suspect not. Might I take this opportunity of showing it to the Defence now so that they can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you first show it to the Defence, then we'll find out whether there's any objection to it. Any objection? No, there's no -- I'm looking at all three counsel. There's no objection to show this to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No, no, no. Could a copy be shown to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Have you seen that insignia or symbol or design before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, I saw it at the police station for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And what about on Mr. Shalja? You talked about insignia that he had. Is it similar to that? Don't just nod. You need to speak, give an answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, that's the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I tender that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this would be Exhibit Number P9, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's a full exhibit, isn't it, if Your Honours please? If Your Honours please, that's a full exhibit now in the case, I understand; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is not yet admitted. This Chamber often takes decisions on admission at the very end. Here it -- since there was no objection, but the specific problem here was it wasn't disclosed to the Defence in advance, so I only asked whether there was any objection of showing it to the witness. Admission, we'll deal with that at the very end. All these numbers are now marked for identification, an admission decision will be taken. We usually do that not one by one but at the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Certainly. I understand. Very well. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When Mr. Shalja was giving his speech, were there any tractors or vans nearby?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: There were a little further away from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was there anything on or in those vans or tractors?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: The tractor was covered with a tarpaulin and I couldn't look in the van to see what was inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. In the village of Junik, I think you said there were Roma or Egyptian families living there; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did -- and about how many would you say were resident in Junik back in May of 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Ten to 12 houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And just for Their -- so Their Honours understand, that's 10 to 12 houses, but each house might have a number of Roma or Egyptian people living in those houses, extended families; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Following this episode where Mr. Shalja gave his speech, did the Roma families do anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to object to that as being vague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio -- yes, of course, vague questions are usually not leading; that's one of the advantages. But I do understand that you ask Mr. Di Fazio to be a bit more specific. Could you reformulate your question, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Mr. Guy-Smith for assisting me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did the Roma families continue to reside in the village after the speech by Mr. Shalja?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When did they leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: The same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you actually see them leaving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you make any inquiries or try and find out why they were leaving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What sort of inquiries did you make and what did you find out, if anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: We were asking them why they were leaving, and they said that the whole town was already full of weapons and people were frightened and they wanted to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did any other ethnic groups also depart at the same time that the Roma and Egyptian families were departing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, you didn't -- you didn't go, did you? I think you remained for some time in Junik; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell the Trial Chamber why you - you and your family - didn't leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Well, I thought that I was a decent person, that I had done no harm to anybody, and I didn't see any reason why I should leave my home.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, how long did you remain in Junik before finally leaving, following this episode where Mr. Shalja gave his speech?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Very shortly after my window was broken by that stone, I went to see the leader of the democratic party to complain and tell him what had happened to me. And he advised me to spend some time, and especially the night, away from my home, to go to some friends or family, but only a day later the war broke out in Junik.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Just think about this question that I'm going to ask you now, please. Take your time in answering it. Cast your mind back to 1998, in May. Think about how things happened over days, and so on. You said that Shalja gave a speech and he had insignia on his uniform; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You remember that. You were there. You heard him give his talk; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, at the time that he gave his talk and you're there listening to him, had the rock been thrown through your window? Was it then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: That night, when the weapons were brought, that same night a rock was thrown through my window. When they had already moved away, somebody threw a rock through my window.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay, all right. How long after Mr. Shalja gave his speech that you went to hear did you go and speak to the democratic party man? About how long after that, would you say? Was it hours, days, weeks? How long?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Several hours after that rally was over.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Anyway, one thing is clear in your mind, is that the sequence of events is this: The rock was thrown at your window --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: At this point, objection. Asked and answered. We've now been through rocks and windows on a number of occasions. She's --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Di Fazio. On a number of occasions. I think the sequence is quite clear. The record speaks for itself. I don't believe Mr. Di Fazio necessarily has received the answer that he wants, but that's an entirely different matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I have heard the answers and I know them, and I think these --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you just want to repeat the answers, then the Chamber is in a position to read the answers, so that's -- and we have heard the answers as well. Unless it is a necessary introduction for your next question, but -- please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, timing is all important, and it's not a question of me trying to rectify any answers that have been given. I've heard all the answers, and I've heard what the witness has said, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You've mentioned certain events, the rock-throwing episode and going to speak to the leader of the democratic party, and you've also mentioned war. How long after you speaking to the democratic party man did war break out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Another 24 hours later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you take the advice and go and stay with friends, the advice of the democratic party man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did your family also go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, except my father and my step-mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What did they do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: They stayed at the apartment, and I went to my neighbours to spend the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You spent the entire night there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What happened the next morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: The next morning, around 7.00, shooting started, targeting the house of that neighbour where I was spending the night, and the fire was so strong that we couldn't even dart outside to get the firewood to light some fire or to get some food.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned the war starting. Was this shooting -- as far as you could tell, as far as you could tell, was this associated with what you call "the war starting" or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It was fighting between the police and the KLA. It was very fierce fighting and there was fire at our house, the house where I was staying.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. And what was the reaction of you and your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Well, it was bad for us. We had no choice -- in fact, I had no choice but to crawl to my apartment to get my personal documents and to get my clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did your family also crawl with you back to your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You've mentioned the war starting and you've mentioned shooting at the house that you were in, the place where you had gone to stay overnight. Was that all rifle fire or automatic weapons fire, small-arms fire, as far as you could tell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: It was mainly from automatic rifles and light weapons, but there were also very strong hits.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was there anything, as far as you could tell, that sounded to you at least like heavy-weapon fire, cannons, or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I think it was mainly shells, those shells from RPGs. I don't know much about that, but I know the approximate name for an RPG rifle-propelled grenade and that when it hits the house, the whole house shakes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. You and your family made it back to your house. What happened there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I came to fetch my ID and to put on some clothes, but we had no time, really. Men in camouflage came with black balaclavas and two civilians with them. I know for a fact there were four of them and they came into my apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, I'll ask you about them in just a moment. Now, just before they arrived, which members of your family were gathered there? Now, remember, don't use any of their names; just tell us who they were. To start off, was your father there, for example?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: There was my father, my step-mother, my sister-in-law, my sister, two children of my brother, myself. The children were small, my brother's children were small. And there was also my aunt and my cousin.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did your aunt -- was your aunt married? If she was, was her husband there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No, no, she was already a widow by that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Now, you've told us that some men arrived. You've told us they had black balaclavas and two civilians and that they were wearing camouflage. Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No, not those who were masked. They looked familiar, but I couldn't tell who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What about -- what about the other men who were not masked? Did you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No, but they were from the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I know because I'd never seen them in Junik.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Now, at about this time that you've got back to your house, you've crawled back to your house and the masked men arrive, were civilians in the town of Junik doing anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were they behaving in any particular way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: They had left their homes and formed a column, a convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And you've told us that you live near the main street. Was this column anywhere near the main street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When you went back to your house, when you went back to your house with your family on your hands and knees, but before the KL -- let me withdraw that question. When you went back to your house but before the men in camouflage uniforms came to your house, did you have any plans? Did you have an idea about what you wanted to do, what you were going to do about the situation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: My thinking was that I should go out, too, and join the convoy with my family, because I had already been told by the president of the democratic party that -- in fact, he said to me, When I go with my family, you and yours will go, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll just finish off this topic, if Your Honours please, and then would it be an appropriate time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It would be an appropriate time for a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Could I just have another two or three minutes, and I'll finish this topic off, if that's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, let's get back to the men in camouflage uniforms. When they came in, did they say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Tell us, what did they say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: "Come on, get out and join our column. Get out of your apartment. It seems that somebody in your building was killed."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness's microphone went off in the middle of this answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we just check the microphone of the witness and ... Witness 38, we heard there was a little problem with your microphone. Could you say a few words in order to test the microphone, whether it's functioning well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, of course. No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I was just asking you to tell us what the camouflage -- the men in camouflage uniform said to you, and you told us before your microphone ceased to function that they said: "Come on, get out, join our column. Get out of your apartment. It seems that somebody in your building was killed." Did they say anything more than -- just listen. Hang on. Did they say anything more beyond that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: They said, Somebody was killed in your apartment and stay all together, your entire family, and don't move away from the column. Somebody was killed up there in the loft. Stick together, all of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you join the column?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And were the armed men in camouflage uniform with you, or take you to the column, or did they leave? How was it -- what did they do after they gave you these instructions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No, they stayed at the apartment and climbed up to the loft to fight, and one of them just escorted us to the column.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And just before we -- the very last question: Your apartment, was it -- or house, was it in an apartment block or was it a single, free-standing house? What sort of place was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No. It's a building, a military-owned building, in the centre of Junik. It was known as the military building. There were six flats on three storeys, and there was a loft.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 38, we'll have a break. I'll first ask Madam Usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll break for approximately half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, one question for you. You spent until now 57 minutes examining this witness. The witness was scheduled for one hour and a half. Do you think you will -- I'm looking at your list, the filed list, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, I know, Your Honour. I'm, unfortunately, going slower than I thought I would. I can't finish this witness in that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time do you think you would need?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Another hour and a quarter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll consider the matter over the break. Of course, the concern of the Chamber is that an assessment of times it takes to examine the witness and -- to be quite honest, the witness is responding to your questions, so I do not know what made you expect that it would be far quicker than -- because it should be far quicker. If you need another one hour and a quarter, that's two hours and a quarter, that's approximately 50 per cent more time. I don't know. It's not entirely clear to me what made you expect that this witness would testify in a different speed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's not, perhaps, discuss it at this moment. We'll consider the matter. We'll have a break until a quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 38, we have a bit of a later start. I was informed that you find it not easy, which is quite understandable. It's perhaps your first experience in a courtroom, so it's fully understood. If you feel not at ease, please tell me, just let me know, and we'll find a solution in whatever way. Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No need for apologies. Mr. Di Fazio, the Chamber would like to encourage you to see whether you could finish in some 60 minutes. You're encouraged to do that. And you know the Prosecution has been granted time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I've performed some surgery on my notes. So I hope that will -- I hope that will do the trick.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then Mr. Di Fazio will now continue his examination. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Witness, before the break, we were talking about the convoy that you saw and your joining the convoy. Did you join the convoy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes. They told me to join the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is there any --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, you had such a nice routine before the break, switching off your microphone, but you seem to have forgotten about it. Please --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I will do my utmost to remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is there an area of Junik called Gaciferi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did the convoy go to Gaciferi or via Gaciferi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: It went towards Gacifer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you remain with the convoy after you joined it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I remained with them until the very centre of Junik, as far as that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you ever leave the convoy or column?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No. I asked to go in the direction of Rastavica, but they would not let me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who prevented you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: One of the KLA members.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did your passage in the convoy take you anywhere near Gaciferi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did anything happen at Gaciferi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: They told me to go in the house of Qazim Gaciferi.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Hold it there, please. At this point of time, did you see any vehicles anywhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What vehicles did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I saw different vehicles, and there was a jeep among them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, you said: "They told me to go in the house of Qazim Gaciferi." Who is "they"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: KLA members.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did you go to the house of Mr. Gaciferi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was that your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Sorry, I'll be clear. Was your family - your family - did that -- did your family leave the convoy and go to the house of Mr. Gaciferi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you have any names of anyone who told you to leave the convoy and go to this house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who gave you instructions or who told you to do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Nimon Tofa and Muharem Knushi, aka Giqa.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you remember how they were dressed at the time that they instructed you to leave the convoy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Muharem, called Giqa, was in a black camouflage uniform, but this other guy, he was still in civilian clothes but he had an automatic rifle in his hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You've mentioned your family was taken out of the convoy. Were there any other people - and I don't want to hear their names - but were there any other people of Roma ethnicity or Egyptian ethnicity who were taken out of the convoy?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Leading. I think he can ask were any other people taken out of the convoy and then find out who those people were, as opposed to suggesting a particular kind of person or ethnic group that may have been taken out of the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'll rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When you were taken out of the convoy, were any other people taken out of the convoy with you, apart from you and your family -- in addition to you and your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What ethnicity were those people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Romas.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was it your choice to be -- to leave the convoy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No, no. We were ordered to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did you finally -- did you make your way to the Gaciferi house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, at the Gaciferi house, you've told us that your family was taken out of the convoy and other Romas were and taken to this house. Did you see any soldiers at this house? Now, you've already told us about Tofa and the other man Giqa. Now, apart from Tofa and Giqa, were there any other soldiers at the Gaciferi house that you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: When we entered at that moment, no, but some arrived a bit later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Names? Do you have any names for those people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I'm trying to remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's all right. If you can't remember, that's fine. Can you -- do you have any memory of the names; if not, don't worry about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm so sorry. Just before Mr. Di Fazio continues, that question, "Do you have any names," I wonder if he would be kind enough at each stage to break down the question by asking the witness whether there was anybody who she knew prior to that event and knew their name, rather than simply saying, "Do you have any names," so the foundation can be laid for the witness' knowledge of the name that she's using.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I understand that; I understand Mr. Emmerson's concerns. I know what he's driving at, and I can certainly accommodate him. But the episode that I'm actually -- what I thought I was dealing with here is not the episode that he is concerned with. But I understand his worries and I'll deal with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so. Witness 38, these are legal, procedural matters you don't have to worry about. Just listen and give your answers. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You've told us that you saw some cars in the vicinity of the Gaciferi house and one of those cars you described as a jeep. Did you see that jeep again after the first time you laid eyes on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, I did another time by the mill.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How far -- just relax, Witness. You're doing very well. I know you're doing your best to try to answer my questions, and it's a strange environment, but you just do your best; all right? How far was the mill -- how far was the mill, approximately, from the Gaciferi house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Well, approximately half a kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you go to the mill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, we did, in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was that your family as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, I went there myself with my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And you also mentioned earlier that some other people of Roma ethnicity had been taken from the convoy with you to the Gaciferi house, people in addition to your family. Were they also -- did they go to the mill or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: They came quite a bit later, after I had arrived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, let's concentrate on the period of time between the Gaciferi house and the mill; all right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were you free to move your hands in the time that -- in between the Gaciferi house and the mill? Could you move your hands?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Up to the mill, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were you clothed between the time that you moved from the Gaciferi house to the mill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, I was, to the mill, up to the mill.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right, thank you. Now, you've told us that you and your family went to the mill, and you've also told us that you saw a jeep there. Before I ask you any more about the car, I'd like to ask you about what happened to you, if anything happened to you, at the mill. Was your father with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: My father, my sister, my entire family, were with me. And if I can answer your question in terms of what happened at the mill --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to ask you that. Just let me ask you a question first.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you have any financial booklet, any book dealing with financial matters, with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, I had it among my personal papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Your father, was he wearing a moustache at the time? Sorry, did he have a moustache at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, he did have a moustache.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, are you able to go on? You sure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, I want you to tell the Trial Chamber, tell the Judges, what happened to you and your father at the mill.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: After we arrived at the mill, a member of the KLA named Aslan Luluni walked up to us and he started mistreating us, first me. He had me undress, and he rummaged through my bag and my personal documents, and he found my bank-book. He tore it in half, and he had me swallow one half of the book. Then he grabbed my father, and he pulled him by the moustache, and he pulled out half of his moustache, right there on the spot.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours, but I just can't bear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Luluni, can you remember how he was dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: He was in a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, when Mr. Luluni walked up to you, was he in company with anyone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes. The nephew of Nimon Tofa was there, the guy I mentioned a while ago. It was actually the son of his brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Anyone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No. This jeep drove up a bit later to that spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You'd mentioned the jeep driving up a bit later. In relation to what was happening to you and your father, the forced removal of your clothes and your father's moustache, those events, in relation to those events, when did the jeep appear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: After they had tied my hands and my father's hands with barbed wire and left me there, naked as I was, and after they had beaten up my father, some ten minutes later, the jeep arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was your father tied?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What was the weather like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: It was raining heavily. It was very bad weather.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And where was the remainder of your family, apart from you and your father?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: They were there but a bit farther away from that spot, 4 or 5 metres. My sister-in-law actually took her children a bit away so that they wouldn't see what was being done to me and my father.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were you, your father, and the remainder of your family, and the children, exposed to the remain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes. We were outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When you and your father were tied, were you close to each other, or can you tell us how far apart you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Well, they were a bit off, a bit farther from that spot, from me and my -- where I and my father were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You tell me if I'm right. I just want to understand your evidence. Were you and your father close together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. So the picture that you've just painted of you and your father tied up in the rain, with the remainder of your family some distance away, in relation to that period of time, when did the jeep arrive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: After some 15 or 20 minutes, at most.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's -- I want to ask you about the jeep. Were there people -- obviously, there was a driver, but was it just a driver or were there other people in the jeep?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, my question --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No, there were other people, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Tell the Trial Chamber who was in the jeep.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Aslan -- no, sorry, Knushi, called Giqa, and Ramush Haradinaj were in the jeep.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just cast your mind back, okay, and tell us what you saw. Okay, just tell us what you saw. How many men in the jeep?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I cannot recall exactly whether there were three or four of them, but I saw those who left the jeep, who got out of the jeep, with my own eyes; Muharem and Ramush, although I had not known them before.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The man you called -- the man you refer to or call Ramush, had you ever seen him before up until that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: That's right. No, I had not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Let's talk about Muharem first. How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: It was a camouflage uniform. Basically, it was all black.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The time that you -- the jeep stopped and you say these men got out, how far away was that from you and your father?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Some 30 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. What did the men who got out of the jeep do once they first got out of the jeep?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: They talked to Aslan Luluni who had tied our hands before that and who had mistreated us before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thinking back, about how far away from you were this group of men when they started talking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Well, approximately 20 or 30 metres. Perhaps a bit more than that. I cannot recall because I was very traumatised at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, all right. Now, you said that there was a man there who you ascribed the name Ramush Haradinaj to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You hadn't seen that man up until that point of time; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: That's correct. No, I hadn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: This man that you call Ramush Haradinaj, what was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you remember any other features about his clothing or anything that he had with him? Anything at all? Any pieces of equipment? Anything that you can recall will be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I remember he had a radio with him, a cap on his head, two of those badges stuck into his pocket in the shape of the letter V.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Could you hear any of the conversation that was going on amongst these men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I couldn't hear because they were talking on the radio, but I know that Aslan turned towards me again and started abusing me very badly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Doing what, precisely?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: He was beating me with his rifle butt. He was cursing me all the way, mentioning Milosevic and Mircic, saying, If Milosevic doesn't come to rescue you, nobody will, and things like that. And that's how he was talking to me all the way, and my father.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Just so the Trial Chamber understands this evidence, you mentioned a name that he was mentioning Mircic. Just a minute. Just a minute, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It might be an idea if we go into private session just very briefly, Your Honours. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. While Luluni was beating you on this occasion, that last occasion you've just described when he was mentioning these persons' names, Milosevic and so on, where was the man that you -- you say was Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Somebody called him. The jeep stopped immediately. In fact, he left and Aslan Luluni stayed and this relative of Nimon Tofa.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I understand that, but what I want to know is this: You've described that Luluni had already done bad things to you and your father and then, as I understand your evidence, he did other things -- there was a second episode where he did bad things, using the rifle-butt and so on. Now, on this second occasion when he used the rifle-butt and beat you, at that point of time, was the man that you know as Ramush Haradinaj, or you say is Ramush Haradinaj, was he present or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: The first time we were beaten he wasn't there. Later he -- later the beating stopped. Then the jeep appeared, and the man who was beating us stopped and went to the jeep.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Tell us this: When you saw the man that you say was Ramush Haradinaj, were your hands tied?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And your father's?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Very well. I'm going to jump ahead -- I'll withdraw that question. Did you ever see the man you say is -- was Ramush Haradinaj again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Only on TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: About how long after this episode was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Between three and a half and four months, because I was very, very ill.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What sort of television programmes did you see him on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Albanian TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How often did you see him on Albanian TV?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Every other day, or once in three days, or maybe even more often. Every time there would be a news bulletin, he would be on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Going back to the scene now where you're tied up with barbed wire, about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, there are a few matters which are not entirely clear to me, and I'd like to seek clarification from the witness. I have a few matters which are not entirely clear to me. You were asked about the man you called Ramush Haradinaj, about what he was wearing, and then you were also asked about conversation going on amongst these men. Then you said: "I couldn't hear because they were talking on the radio." When you said that, you were referring to the man who had arrived in the jeep or ...?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I meant to say that he was talking on the radio, this hand-held radio he had with him. Who he was talking to, I can't possibly know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And when you say "he," you meant the man you called Ramush Haradinaj before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that moment I didn't know because I hadn't seen him before, but from that time on I saw him frequently on TV and I knew that it was him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you also said -- you said: "I couldn't hear because they were talking on the radio," and then your answer continued, where you said: "But I know that Aslan turned towards me again and started abusing me very badly." You remember that answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, a couple of minutes -- couple of minutes later -- I'm just trying to find it. Yes. A couple of minutes later, when you were asked about whether the man you called Ramush Haradinaj was present or not, you said the following. You said: "The first time we were beaten he wasn't there. Later," you said, "later, the beatings stopped. Then the jeep appeared and the man who was beating us stopped and went to the jeep." Now, the part of the answer I referred to earlier says, I couldn't follow this radio conversation and then Aslan, I think you said Aslan, turned to me again, beating you again. In this portion of the answer, the later answer, you said: "The first time we were beaten, he wasn't there and the beating stopped when the jeep appeared." Now, I hope you understand that I have to see whether the beatings stopped at all when the jeep appeared, as your later answer suggests a bit, or whether what you said earlier, that the jeep arrived, there was some radio conversation and that then one of these persons, I think you called him Aslan, went again to you, started beating again. Now, what was it? Was the beating stopped at the time the jeep arrived and when the person beating you went to the jeep, or did it recommence later, as you said, Aslan came back to me again? So was it recommencing after the arrival of the jeep, when it had, from what I understand, stopped at the arrival of the jeep, or did it not recommence again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, he started beating us again. He went at one point to the jeep, talked to them, and then returned and started beating us for the second time, and the abuse resumed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: During the time that Ramush Haradinaj was there - Haradinaj, I'm sorry, I should pronounce -- I think that's the correct pronunciation - did you have any clothes on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Doing the best you can, how long was Mr. Haradinaj there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Did you eventually leave the area of the mill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, after a lot of fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just return very briefly for one moment. I'm sorry, just one more matter that I want to raise with you. When Mr. Haradinaj was there, how did Aslan Luluni and the other men with him refer to Mr. Haradinaj, if at all? How did they deal with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: As with commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What do you mean by that? I want to understand. Is there something they did that makes you say that, or something you heard, or something they did and something you heard? Why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I heard that's how they addressed him, but what they actually said, I wasn't able to hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And may I also clarify some point concerning this short period of time when the man you called Ramush Haradinaj was there. Was it during this presence, in his presence, that this second beating occurred? Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He had gone by then. He wasn't present when they were beating us. I was naked while being beaten, and the man who beat me stopped for a while to go and see him, and when he returned, he started beating me again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. I would like to move on fairly fast now, if you can assist me, Witness. Did you eventually rejoin the convoy or column?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were you with your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were you clothed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You said you had been tied. Had you been untied -- were you untied before rejoining the convoy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And your father, was he tied or untied when you rejoined the convoy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: He was also tied.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. And which direction was the -- was this column of people headed in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Towards Djocaj, Jesic. That's the direction of Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Later the Judges would like to -- later, they would like to know where these places are. Now, first of all, Djocaj, is that a separate village from Jasic or Jesic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber this: Was the column headed in the general direction of the Albanian border?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you and your group eventually stop and camp overnight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No. We stopped somewhere in the middle of the woods, and it started raining heavily.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What I'd like to -- if you could just briefly give us --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: We didn't get to the camp. We stopped in the middle of the woods.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's apology.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay, all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That night, when you stayed out, what I want to know is was it just your group, or were you part of the convoy that stopped or column that stopped?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No, no. We were separated from the column. The column continued on. We were singled out and left at Jasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, you've told us that you and your father, at least, were tied up. Were you free to leave, to walk away, to go wherever you want to -- you might have wanted to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Not really.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, why not? Tell the Trial Chamber why you weren't free to make your decisions about where to go.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Because we had an escort.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: A member of the KLA, but he was in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. And I just want to be absolutely clear about this. You say he was an escort. Were you at liberty -- did you feel that you could tell your escort that you wanted to leave; you didn't want to be escorted anymore?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: We begged him but he said, I can't let you go. I have my orders. I have to be with you at all times.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You stayed overnight at this location and the next day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did anything happen to your sister the next day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes. A group of men came, wanted to abuse and rape her, but some other men did not let them. And this first group -- in fact the man from the first group who wanted to rape my sister said, Why bother with that one since this one is already naked and ready? But the person who was guarding us didn't let them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you remain in that area for that day and again for a second night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Did your condition remain the same; namely, were you still tied and still naked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I want to now skip the events of the night, the second night in that location, and I want you to take us to the next day. Did you leave your camp site, or your -- the area where you'd been for two nights, and go somewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes. I was allowed to get dressed because I was already getting a fever, and we went -- we set off towards Jasici.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was the man who was your escort -- was your escort still with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Until halfway, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And where -- where did he go after the halfway -- let me rephrase that. Let me withdraw that question. Whose idea was it to set off to Jasici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: He told us to go towards Jasici, up to Aslan Djoci's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were you given any explanation where you were going, why you were going, and whose idea it was that you should go to this place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I don't know who decided it, but they told us to go to Aslan Djoci's house because the headquarters was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Headquarters of what? Headquarters of what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: The KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, who -- when you say: "They told us to go to Aslan Djoci's house," who is "they"? Who do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I mean members of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And so the man who had been escorting you over the previous two days, he left your group; do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, until we got near the house of Aslan Djoci.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you have any other escort from that point onwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No. When we got in, there were a lot of them inside, enough to keep an eye on us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Now, again, just explain to the Trial Chamber who you mean by "them," "a lot of them." A lot of who, precisely?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I mean the KLA army, members of the KLA, or UCK. I mean them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just tell the Trial Chamber a bit about the geography of Aslan Djoci's house. Where -- where, precisely, was it located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: On a hill which is almost as high as a mountain, very close to the Albanian border, almost at the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And there was a house on this hill, is that right, Aslan Djoci's house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, tell the Trial Chamber, the sort of numbers of men that you saw -- the KLA army members that you saw at Aslan Djoci's house. Was it one or two or more than that? Give us a figure, if you can.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: More, more. Lots of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
