utterances.text: Did you see any armaments or weapons there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, tell -- can you give the Trial Chamber any assistance on the amount of weapons that you saw there. Was there -- did all of the KLA men that you saw there have a gun or not? Did you see weapons by themselves? If you can assist, try and give a more accurate description of the amount of weaponry that may -- that you saw there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: There was a lot of weapons there in the -- there was a heap in the middle of the yard. The yard was a big one. Everybody whom I saw there was armed. And then there were quite a few people in the yard, in that area around the house of Aslan Djoci. It was actually the nest where they kept all the weapons which they had brought. They brought it to his house -- to the yard, actually. There were crates, boxes, lying every which way. There were all sorts of things in the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, at this point in time, you were -- were you with your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Let's just run through them again. Again, no names, all right? So your father was there -- just tell us who was there but no names.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: My father was there; I, myself, was there; my step-mother was there; my sister, too; my sister-in-law; and two minor children were with us; seven family members in all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did this house have a back yard or an area at the back of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, it did have, and there were entrances on two sides to the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When you arrived there, where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: We were taken to the house of Riza Djoci, which is the next-door neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Are there a number of houses located on top of this hill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: One could see from those two houses a place called Rastavica, and these two houses were quite near one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And when you were taken to the house of Riza Djoci, at that point were you and your family taken anywhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is there a geographical feature or a ravine or small valley near Riza Djoci's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were you taken anywhere close to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes. We were taken to a place. There is -- near this house there is some sort of a ridge, some sort of an edge, and there we were lined up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: All my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you see any weapons nearby? At that point of time when you were lined up, did you see a weapon nearby?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What sort of weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: It was a machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. I want you to tell us now, in your own words, what happened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Are you talking about what happened in the house of Riza Djoci?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm talking about what happened when you and your family were lined up and there was a machine-gun nearby.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: They told us to stand in a line, to line up one next to another. And there was a boy, a young lad not even of age, and one of those soldiers came and he ordered him to execute us. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: As they quarrelled, someone hit me, kicked me, and I fell down the slope. And then my father rolled after me, and then my family ran down the slope -- down the hill. And we fell to where a river was, and that river -- this water-course is called Erenik, where the place was where we fell. And this is a -- this is a very powerful river, but we fell where there was a smaller water-course nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you and your family make your way to a place called Batusa, I think it is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And there did you come across what were then Yugoslavian army soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did they take you into their custody and -- well, did they take you and your family off to -- off to get some help and assistance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Di Fazio. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would have one or two minor matters perhaps on which I'd like to be sure that I understood your testimony well. First is, again, the same issue. You were beaten, the beating stopped when the jeep arrived, the man who was beating you went to the jeep, there was conversation, then the man returned to you and the beating recommenced. Did I understand you well that those who came in the jeep, one of them you called Ramush Haradinaj, had left already when the beating recommenced? Is that well understood or ...?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Then one other matter. You were asked why you said that the man dealt with Ramush Haradinaj "as with commander," and you said the following. You said: "I heard that's how they addressed him, but what they actually said I wasn't able to hear." What I'd like to know from you, where you said "I heard that's how they addressed him," that could be understood in two different ways; either that you heard these men addressing the man you call Ramush Haradinaj as "Commander," or that you were told by these men or by anyone else that they addressed him, or would address him, as "Commander." Now, did you hear with your own ears these men addressing the man you called Ramush Haradinaj as "Commander" or did you hear later or at the same time from other people that's how they address him? Which of the two is what you meant to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There might have been a mistake there, but one of them addressed him, "Commander." I'm not quite sure, and I apologise. Maybe they didn't address that title to him but to another one; there were two of them there. But I did hear the word -- them say the word "Commander."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you're not certain about whom of the persons that arrived in the jeep was addressed when they used the word "commander"; is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you are right. Maybe they were addressing this other person as commander. There was a man from Junik there who had arrived there with him, Muharem Knushi, Giqa. Maybe that was addressed to him. I only heard a voice say "Commander." And they were addressing them, "Comrade Commander," or "Commander."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for this clarification. Mr. Emmerson, I'm looking at the clock, perhaps -- I take it, since you've announced that you might need a bit more time for cross-examination anyhow, that we'll almost certainly not finish today; that perhaps first have a break because we can continue up to 7.00 from now on.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm happy make a start now, if you would like me to, or we can take a break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll soon have a break, but Judge Hoepfel has one question in which he seeks further clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Witness, may I just ask you for clarification. You and your family, are you from a Roma background yourself? Because you were asked about other Romas and that was not expressly said before, what your own origin is, or background.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am a Roma, but my mother tongue is Albanian, and I was educated in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not quite get the first part of the second portion of the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: The interpreter did not quite get the first part of the second portion of your answer, and, in fact, I would have asked you that anyway; that would have been my second question, about your mother tongue. Can you explain that once more?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Albanian is my mother tongue. I cannot speak the Romani language. Our school was in Albanian, and it is Albanian that I speak better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness 38, we'll have a break. After the break, you'll be examined by counsel for the accused. That will -- we'll not go any further today than 7.00. We most likely will not finish today, but we'll see. We'll have a break until five minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 38, the first counsel that will cross-examine you is Mr. Emmerson, counsel for Mr. Haradinaj. Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 38, I want to ask you, first of all, following up from Judge Hoepfel's question, one or two questions about language. You told us that your mother tongue is Albanian; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You're giving your evidence, I think, in Serbian; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you are fluent in Serbian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you understand any other languages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Just Serbian and Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you don't understand English at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to start by asking you about the incident at the mill at Gacifer when you say that you and your father were stripped naked and beaten, and you were made by Aslan Luluni to eat your pocketbook. You've told us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your bank-book, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your bank-book. You've told us that this happened after you had been beaten and stripped naked, and that a Suzuki jeep then drew up; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: I don't remember having heard of a Suzuki.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems that you're quoting from the statement rather than-- please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me put the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You have told us that you were beaten and stripped naked, and then a jeep drew up after that first beating had taken place; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: We were at the mill. We were not taken there in a jeep, but we were there. That much is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You've told us that you believe that one of the men who drew up in the jeep was Ramush Haradinaj, and I want to make it absolutely clear to you at the outset of the questions I'm going to ask what it is I am suggesting to you. I am suggesting to you that you are wrong and that Ramush Haradinaj was not in Junik or in Gacifer or anywhere near the mill or in a jeep in that vicinity on the 28th of May.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I say that he was with Muharem Knushi. That is what I saw. And later I saw a person on the TV screen, and I believe that he was that person. That could be -- that could not be so only if there is a person that strikingly resembles him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What I want to do now is to go through the account you've given to make sure we're absolutely clear about certain key steps in the order of events. So I'm going to put certain propositions to you from what you've already told us and just seek your clarification as to whether what I'm putting to you accurately represents your evidence. First of all --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- I think you've confirmed that you had already been stripped naked and beaten, and that you had already been made to eat half of your bank-book, and that your hands had been tied before this jeep arrived; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If I say anything that is not right, please take the opportunity to correct it, because I want everybody in this courtroom to be absolutely certain that we know exactly what it is you are saying. When the jeep arrived, you were naked and tied up; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And in the jeep were three men altogether - the driver; a man called Muharem Knushi, who you knew as Giqa; and the man you say was Ramush Haradinaj; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you know Muharem Knushi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Aslan Luluni was not in the jeep when it drew up; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Right

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You're absolutely sure about that, Witness 38?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He was, or had been, beating you and walked over to the jeep when it drew up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He then went to speak to the men in the jeep; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Neither you nor your father were beaten or ill-treated whilst the jeep was in the vicinity; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But as soon as the jeep had gone, Aslan Luluni returned and beat you a second time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: While the jeep was there, you heard some of the men use the word "commander"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Other than that, is it right that you could not hear anything that they were saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No; that is to say, I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So the only word that you made out from these conversations was "commander"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Pardon. This is a very special expression, of course. There might have been other single words which still wouldn't make sense to the witness, wouldn't they? So did you mean, Witness, that you didn't hear any other word or that you didn't make -- that you were not able to understand the sense of what was spoken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I couldn't hear because I was away, and I had been beaten quite a lot and slapped about, and in my ears, too. And I couldn't hear what they were saying because they were talking over the radio-set and using codes and coded words. I couldn't make out what was transpiring between them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So the only word that you understood, let's put it that way, was the word "commander" ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you didn't know for sure which of the two men was being referred to as a commander, Muharem Knushi or the man you say was Ramush Haradinaj? You didn't know which one that word was addressed to; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No. I only heard, that is, the word "commander," and to whom it was addressed of the two, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So it follows from what you've told us that you never heard any of the soldiers present say, "Commander Ramush Haradinaj, this woman is at your disposal," did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you're quite sure about that, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We'll come back to that, if we may, a little later. Did you understand Muharem Knushi to have any particular role in Junik amongst the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No. I always saw that he was in camouflage uniform and that he was brandishing a machine-gun or a light machine-gun - I'm not quite sure - the small machine-gun, in his hands, and everything went through him. People were calling him, asking him things and so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Have you ever told an investigator for the Prosecution that Muharem Knushi was the commander of the Junik KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, this man, you say, you think was Ramush Haradinaj, you can confirm you had never seen him in your life before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think it's right, isn't it, as well, that you had never heard of Ramush Haradinaj before this day, the 28th of May, 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I had not heard of his name; that is to say, I had heard of the Haradinajs but not of Ramush Haradinaj, him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: How long in total was this man in your -- in your vicinity from the time that the jeep arrived until the time that it left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: You mean how -- for how long was he present there?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's my question, yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: For a full 10 minutes, for 10 or 15 minutes or so. He was talking, using the walkie-talkie, and after that he immediately got on the jeep and went off somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And how far away from him were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: About 30 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you see him clearly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I could see him clearly from one side and not facing me, because he was sitting there with his colleague, with this Muharem, and was talking to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you saw him from 30 metres away, on a side view only?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And would he have been able to see you, a naked woman tied up with her naked father, 30 metres from where he was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I don't know. There was this mill on the right side. We were by the mill. There was some sort of a bush there, a rose bush, I believe. Whether he was able to see me, I'm not sure. I don't know. This mill was in the middle of the forest, and there was just a river below, and there was -- there were woods everywhere around it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So there were bushes and woods between where he was and where you were; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you're telling us that because of those bushes and woods, he might not have been able to see you and your naked father 30 metres from where he was; is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Well, it may have been -- it may have been that way. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you're telling us that you, despite those bushes and trees, could clearly see his profile?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, I could see him from one side quite well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you trying to cover yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I could not cover myself. My hands were tied. There was no way I could do it. The family which was there near me dared not do anything because we had two minor children with us and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were you curled up on the floor or were you standing up, naked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No, no, I was sitting on the ground, with our hands tied behind our backs.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: How far away was the fighting at this point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I cannot tell you in terms of metres, but from this place where I was to Rastavica, which is the place where the army and the police was, there -- I don't know how many metres or kilometres were between that place and Rastavica, but I'm sure that there were some kilometres between us.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But, Witness 38, you've told us in your testimony that there was fighting going on in the streets of Junik on the very day that you ended up at the mill, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. But between Rastavica and Junik, there is a hill that the police and army were targeting, and they were shooting from a location in the woods close to Gacifer. There are houses close to the woods, and that's where they were shooting from. And in any case, there was a fierce exchange of fire, a lot of fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you just told us there are houses close to the woods and that there was shooting from a location in the woods close to Gacifer; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: There are a lot of houses there. It's a populated area, a little mahala called Gaciferi. And just overlooking that is a very high hill. And the location where the police and the army were is called Kodra e Rastavices, and the army and the police were close to a settlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Forgive me for pressing this, but it may be of some importance. Was there shooting in the woods around Gacifer or not; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: There was shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Where is the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, it certainly would assist the Chamber to give an exact time frame for that and not just to work on the basis of perhaps understanding, which might not be a shared understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: At the time that you were naked outside the mill, was there shooting in the woods around Gacifer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Where is the mill in relation to Gacifer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Below on the road -- down the road to Jasic. But above Gaciferi is a hill, and the mill is between Tofa and Gaciferi.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So the mill is, is it not, just a few hundred yards from Gacifer -- a few hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you scared, sitting there, that you may be caught up in the fighting that was so close?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: What do you mean, were we afraid? We thought we would never get out of there alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we then go back to this --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Judge Hoepfel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: I'm not sure if this answer reflects what the witness wanted to say. You were not sure if you would get out alive from that situation. Was that because of the fighting in the woods, or was that because of the situation at the spot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were afraid on two counts: Because we were captives on the one hand; and on the other hand, because of the fighting. In any case, we were almost 100 per cent sure that we wouldn't get out of there alive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Coming back to the man you say was Ramush Haradinaj, you've told us that you'd never seen Ramush Haradinaj before and you've told us that you had never heard his name, Ramush Haradinaj, before. So it must follow, mustn't it, that at the time that jeep drove away, you had no means of knowing who the man was that was sitting in the jeep with Muharem Knushi, at the time the jeep drove away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No. But a little later, I had an idea. When I saw him on TV, I realised it was him. But then, back there on the spot, I didn't know his name, I didn't hear his name, nor had I ever seen him before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the television broadcast you say you saw was several months later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we try and work out when that was? I think you said in your testimony in chief it was about three and a half to four months later. Is that your recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, because in the meantime I had been through extensive treatment to recover from all the torture and all that beating, and it was quite a while before I got out of the hospital. In the hospital, I couldn't watch anything. It was only when I got home that I could watch TV, when I returned to Djakovica, that is, because I couldn't go home.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you can be absolutely sure you saw this television broadcast before you left Kosovo for the last time, around the middle of 1999, can you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, before we left as refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: May we go into closed session -- private session for a short moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: By the time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just want to go back. Now, you've mentioned a statement that you've made previously, and I just want to clarify what we're speaking about. I think when you say you came down the hillside after what you say was an attempt to assassinate you at the top of the hill, that you encountered VJ forces, Yugoslav Army forces, on the road; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think you encountered them in a place called Batusa; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You may not know this, but there was a senior Yugoslav Army general there when you arrived, the Chief of Staff of the 125th Battalion, a man called Colonel Dragan Zivanovic, and he heard you give your account of what had happened to you when you first came into the hands of the Yugoslav Army. Did you know Colonel Zivanovic was there when you first spoke to officers of the army, before you made a video interview, the very first contact you had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No, no. No, I did not, nor had I heard the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think after you first spoke to the officers of the Yugoslav Army, you say they then arranged for you to do a video interview to tell them what had happened to you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then after you'd done the video interview, they took you to the MUP and you made a written statement for the MUP at that time, in May -- the beginning of June, I think it would be, 1998; is that right as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, it follows from what you've told us already that you will not have told the VJ or the MUP anything at all about Ramush Haradinaj being present during this incident, will you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Because, of course, at that time you hadn't seen him on the television, had you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you've told us that you told not a soul when you did recognise him on the television at any time between three months after this event, so that would take us to about August, and June the next year when you left Kosovo. So for a period of ten months, you kept this information to yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think that no, just for clarification, is a no, you didn't tell anyone; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Right. I did not tell anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you did have an interview again with the MUP in November 2002, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Closed session for just a moment, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Private session, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, it was an interview with -- at which a police officer that you knew was present, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you please give us his name?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You made a statement. You've told us that you weren't very well, I think, at that time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we please see briefly the statement that you made. It is Defence document ID 1382 in the English version and 1376 in Serbian. And all exhibits marked for identification during this cross-examination, I have agreed, should remain confidential because they all potentially could carry ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that means that it's not to be shown on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, it may be of assistance if the usher were to guide the witness to the B/C/S version of the statement whilst the rest of us have it in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What I'd like you to do is, if you will, to move down the page to the second page and to a paragraph beginning: "At about 1800 hours ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, I'd like to give a number to this. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit number D1, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we just -- in fact, whilst we're on the first page, if we just cast our eyes down to the second paragraph, beginning: "A KLA member ..." Can you see a reference in that paragraph to the names of Mahalu Gaciferi and Nimon Tofaj? At the bottom of the screen now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Those were names that you were able to remember during this interview, despite the fact that you were feeling unwell, aren't they? Yes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if we can just look to the next paragraph on the following page, beginning: "President of LDK ..." I think it may be -- I think it's at the very top, in fact. We have, unfortunately, a marker over the top of it. We can see -- can you see the name Ruzhdi Sehu, or Sehu Ruzhdi, there and Sinan Sehu? Can you see that? Top of the page, second line down.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And a little further down Sinan Sehu, yes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is part of your narrative and you were explaining there, I think, the names of people who had been present in Junik in the early part of this account; yes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you were able to remember their names despite your illness; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And if we just go down a little further on that paragraph, I think you there mention Cazim Bajrami and Bajram Hodza, who interrupted a conversation that was taking place at that stage; yes? Do you see those? Let me guide you. In the paragraph that you can see on the screen at the moment, the top paragraph, four lines up from the bottom --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "Cazim Bajrami," yes, and "Bajram Hodza," yes. Do you see those names? The arrow is pointing to it now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, I see it. I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so you were able to remember those names, despite your illness, yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: You mean after the sentence --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here, excuse me, Cazim Bajrami, I see it, but for the life of me, I can't remember anymore who Cazim Bajrami was, although I did mention him. But From what I recollect now, I couldn't repeat those names. I know I was in the house of Qazim Gaciferi, but about Bajrami I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The point is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: May I interrupt. You are speaking of the sentence after the sentence: "I do not know this man's name," referring to a man who was mentioned before, "but I think that they told me that his village," and so on. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And then --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then the names appear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: -- the names. But this doesn't have to do with the sentence before. These are different people --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: -- and she's now wondering why she had the recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The point, Witness 38, is that you remembered those individuals' names who were not central to your account at that time despite your illness, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did remember it, but I truly don't remember now. I can't explain now how I came to mention them and who these people were. It's quite possible that immediately afterwards I remembered, but it's -- the whole thing was quite a big shock and a trauma to me. I see that I must have mentioned them. I see that it's written, Cazim Bajrami and Bajram Hodza. Bajram Hodza I know; he's a man from Junik. But about Cazim Bajrami, I really can't say that I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you look at the next paragraph, you remember exactly the very precise time that this incident began at the -- in the lead-up to what happened at the mill, because you refer to seeing Muharem Knushi at 6.00 p.m. Can you see that, 1800, you remembered seeing Muharem Knushi? Do you see that? It's in the -- it's the paragraph that you can see on the page --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yeah, I see it. I see him here, 1800 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just read it quickly over to yourself.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, okay. So you remembered his name and the time that you saw him with some precision, despite your illness, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And what do you say, halfway down the paragraph, about his role in Junik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: It's very hard to read because half of this copy is illegible.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you see the word "radio station," "radio stanice," four lines down in the middle of the paragraph. Do you see that word, "radio station," yes? Where the arrow is pointing now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we just move along a few words, yes, can you see the word "commandant"? It's on the same line. Yes. Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: It's poorly legible, but I think that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Our translation reads: "I know that he was a KLA commander in the village of Junik."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: I can't remember saying that he was the commander. It was too soon after the war began, and I didn't know exactly who was soldier and who was commander. And at that time I couldn't really tell and wasn't able to explain it to them. I couldn't have. This is very odd.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You signed this witness statement on every page, Witness 38, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I suppose we'll need a redaction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the redaction will be made. Mr. Emmerson, I am aware that asking you to find a suitable moment, next you might say there's no suitable moment in the next one or two minutes, but nevertheless we have to stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, whether this would be as bad as any other moment --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If I might --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- just run on for one minute or two. I can probably complete this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I need one minute for procedural minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Then one minute is my limit.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 38, you say in this statement that it was Muharem Knushi who directed you to go to the mill, and you describe the assault by Aslan Luluni; but you make no mention whatsoever of Ramush Haradinaj or, indeed, of a jeep pulling up, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: While we were in Gaciferi, the jeep -- the jeep of that - what's his name? - Muharem Knushi was not there but it did go towards the mill. He said, You go from this house over there and take the direction of the mill.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 38, we need to break now, but let me finish with this. We can all read the statement. You can read the statement. You did not tell the police in 2002 anything at all about knowing that Ramush Haradinaj was there, did you? Did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I didn't mention him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And this was despite the fact that you'd known and seen him every other day on the television since August 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/38
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I hope that will be a suitable point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Emmerson. Witness 38, there will be more questions for you. We'll continue tomorrow, in the afternoon, a quarter past 2.00. Take your time, rest well, and I would like to instruct you that you should not speak to anyone about the testimony you have given today or perhaps testimony still to be given tomorrow. Don't speak with anyone. We'd like to see you back tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I won't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, is there any update on the matter we -- well, we didn't discuss, but I asked you about before?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If Your Honours are referring to the UNMIK --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. We will -- we have obtained some provider permission in relation -- under Rule 70 in relation to the Skender Kuqi files and we will be disclosing some information tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that all the material that was provided under Rule 70 relevant for this case, or is there still a portion not -- I just want to know whether we have now complete permission or --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Not quite.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not quite.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Still working on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We're getting there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'd like to be updated, and I take it that you'll inform the Defence immediately about what is now available, and of course they might be more interested in what is not available. I don't think we've come any further at this very moment. Let's first see what happens after you've given it to the Defence. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. At some point in time, the way that this is proceeding, I believe that a motion is going to need -- is, of necessity, going to have to be filed. I don't know when that's going to be, and I keep on holding back because I'm hoping we can work this out in a much more amicable fashion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you think the time is there for a motion, we'll see a motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's appreciated that you don't hurry into motions where other solutions are still feasible. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, simply this: I just wanted to mention some estimate of how long I'm likely to be, because this is a document-heavy cross-examination. We're really only a little way into the document part of the analysis. And I think I had indicated from the outset that this was a witness that I was likely to be some time with. I would expect cross-examination of about another hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's understood. You announced that you would take a bit more time on this witness. May I, at the same time, ask your attention for the following: Sometimes you refer to matters that certainly are not yet part of the testimony of the witness, such as the 28th of May, where the witness said the 6th or the 7th of May, mid-May, the 6th or the 7th. And I think it's not the only time. For example, the video interview, the witness had not yet confirmed that there had been ever a video interview. You mentioned it, she -- in her answer she didn't confirm it, and then you continued on the video interview. I'd like -- it's not dramatic, but I'd very much like to avoid whatever possible confusion, and while quoting matters that are not yet part of the testimony of the witness, there is at least a risk and these are examples that might not be very dangerous ones, but at least there's a risk of confusion which I'd very much like to avoid.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll study the transcript, and if there are important matters that occur to me that I didn't get a clear enough answer to, I will put them in straight first thing in the morning. I thought she had answered yes in relation to the video interview. If I'm wrong about that, then I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I had the answer -- the videolink was mentioned in a rather long phrase in which a lot of things appeared, among others the video interview, and then of course even if you get a kind of an information, you don't know what is confirmed and what is not confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll break the question down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll adjourn until tomorrow, quarter past 2.00, in the same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 9th day of March, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.05 p.m.,
